packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, one packet per session, prompt and images only (reader brief of PR #76/#77); repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; reread of packets whose first readings were written after the session's image limit had removed earlier images
text:
packet-12 - blind image reading (unverified)
Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or earlier reading of this packet.

LAYOUT SURVEY

Face 1 (overview image-001.jpg, reduced): a bare wooden board (book cover board), grain vertical,
with metal fittings/nails at top-right and bottom-right corners. Only a narrow vertical strip of
parchment is visible along the right edge (roughly x 630-745 of the overview, y ~270-1380). On the
strip: line-initial word fragments in a dark brown/black gothic book hand, each preceded above by
small neumes (dots/strokes) and with red horizontal lines (staff lines or red F-lines) visible above
several text lines. Interpretation (tentative): a strip of a noted liturgical manuscript (text with
musical notation above it), only the left (or right) margin end of each line visible; the parchment
appears turned 90 degrees or the strip is a column edge. One red initial visible near y~1280.
Pencil shelfmark-like note on wood near bottom (not transcribed, modern).
Tiles 002-009 (2 columns x 4 rows) are native-resolution views of this face; text only in the
right-hand tiles.

Face 2 (overview image-010.jpg, reduced): the other side of the same wooden board (outer side),
with remains of leather/parchment covering adhesive, grey ground, and five metal strap/clasp
fittings along the right edge. No writing visible at overview scale. Tiles 011-018 cover this face;
I did not open them because the overview shows no script (to conserve the image budget).

Face 3 (overview image-019.jpg, reduced): detached parchment fragments laid out on black:
 (A) a long narrow vertical strip at left (overview x ~120-240, y ~140-1440), cut from a noted
     manuscript: alternating rows of neumes (black square/dot notation) over single red lines,
     and text lines in a dark brown gothic textualis; red text (rubrics) and one large red
     initial "P" (overview y ~650). Only the left-hand ~6-10 letters of each text line survive.
     Modern pencil "Stams, STA, Frg 257 ..." near its foot.
 (B) five small, badly holed fragments (middle column x ~380-610: three pieces at y ~235-495,
     680-920, 1080-1290; right column x ~750-1040: two pieces at y ~250-520 and 775-920), all
     with the same layout (text line under red line with neumes), heavily abraded, with brown
     adhesive/board residue. Each carries a modern pencil "Stams, STA, Frg 257 .." number.
 Interpretation (tentative): leaves of a noted chant book (antiphoner-type layout with
 "alleluia" and "Euouae" differentiae visible at overview scale), used as binding waste.
Tiles 020-031 (3 columns x 4 rows, native resolution, overlapping) cover this face.

Face 4 (overview image-032.jpg, reduced): the reverse sides of the same six pieces, mirrored in
position (long strip now at x ~140-250; small pieces at x ~380-615 and ~780-1075). Same layout:
text lines under red lines with neumes; red rubric letters; the strip shows a red initial at
y ~1160. The upper-right piece shows the most legible text line at its top
("...gnū ... dulces cla..." at overview scale). Pencil "Stams, STA, Frg 257 .." numbers.
Tiles 033-044 (3 x 4) cover this face.

Reading plan: face 3 strip (A) first (best preserved), then the small pieces on face 3 and 4,
then the face-1 strip on the board. Strip images below are my own crops of the native tiles
(saved under responses-rerun/crops/packet-12/), so line numbers refer to the crop file named.

=====================================================================
FACE 3, STRIP (A)  -- crops of native tiles, x 30-580 of each tile
=====================================================================
Script/notation notes: gothic textualis, brown-black ink, letters ~8 mm tall (large chant-book
module). Notation: black neumes (Gothic/"Hufnagel"-type nail-shaped and square/rhomboid notes)
around a red line, with a faint yellowish line also visible above some text lines (a second,
coloured staff line?). The strip is trimmed on BOTH sides: the left edge cuts through letters,
so the surviving text is a mid-line window ~6-10 letters wide, not line beginnings.
One text line per red line; neume rows between.

f3strip-020.jpg (from tile image-020.jpg; top of strip). Top ~280 px: blank parchment with brown
adhesive stain and a hole; one neume group above the first red line.
 f3strip-020 l.580  : ]n amabilis[   (n at left edge cut; "amabili" + long s, last letter cut by edge)
 f3strip-020 l.860  : ]um nunc[      (first letter partly cut: "um"; final c at the torn edge)
 f3strip-020 l.1140 : ]ua pre[       ("ua" or "ia", first stroke cut; "pre" then torn edge)
 (neumes above each line; below l.1140 another red line with neumes, text below it continues in
  the next tile.)

f3strip-023.jpg (from tile image-023.jpg). Overlap: its top neume row on a red line (l.~100)
is the same as the bottom neume row of f3strip-020 (l.~1270); not new text.
 f3strip-023 l.~230 : (no text visible below that neume row; blank parchment between it and the
                       next red line - either no text here or entirely faded)
 f3strip-023 l.540  : ]sus iohann[   (long-s forms: "ſuſ iohann"; first letter cut by left edge;
                                       last letters at torn right edge)
 f3strip-023 l.820  : ]t alleluia [?](final trace at right edge, a round letter, perhaps E? or e?)
 f3strip-023 l.1110 : P ater [       (large red initial P, about two lines tall, standing in the
                                       left part of the strip with its bowl beside the neume row;
                                       "ater" in black, first a with a red touch? then a partial
                                       letter at the right edge, possibly n/m [illegible])
 f3strip-023 l.1380 : ]bi nunc [     (first letter cut: "bi" or "hi"; "nunc", then trace at edge)
 (neume rows on red lines at l.~390, ~700, ~960, ~1240/1300, ~1520; red line at l.1300 is offset
  rightwards from the one at l.1240 - two short red line segments at different heights, i.e. the
  red line steps.)

f3strip-026.jpg (from tile image-026.jpg). Overlap: top line (l.~40) "]bi nunc[" = f3strip-023
l.1380, not new.
 f3strip-026 l.350  : ]uia Euoua[    (first letter cut, "uia"/"ıa"; "E" in red, "uoua" black, last
                                       letter at the edge with a red/brown trace; read Euoua[e])
 f3strip-026 l.620  : ]alleluia [red letter][ (after "alleluia" a red long s / p-like letter with
                                       a hairline stroke, then edge. Rubric letter, perhaps a
                                       psalm/verse cue mark: [illegible] - I do not expand it)
 f3strip-026 l.910  : ]altum all[    ("altum" - a/l at the left edge partly cut; "all" then edge)
 f3strip-026 l.1200 : Euouae S[      ("E" with red touch, "uouae" black, then a red capital S and
                                       a following partial black letter at the torn edge - n? i?)
 f3strip-026 l.1480 : ]e. adorem[    (a letter + punctus at left edge, then "adorem", final minims
                                       at torn edge)
 (neume rows on red lines at l.~190, ~520, ~860, ~1140, ~1420; faint yellow line under each neume
  row at l.~420, ~760, ~1050, ~1330)

f3strip-029.jpg (from tile image-029.jpg). Overlap: l.~130 "]e. adorem[" = f3strip-026 l.1480.
 f3strip-029 l.440  : ]tua sup[      (first letter t? partly cut; "tua", then long-s "ſup", torn edge)
 Below l.~500: blank parchment (lower margin), brown adhesive residue at foot. Modern pencil
 (vertical): "Stams, STA, Frg. 257-2r" (modern, not part of the text).
 So the strip on face 3 is the last ~11 text lines of a column plus lower margin; top has an
 upper blank area of ~250 px (upper margin?) before the first neume row.

SUMMARY of face 3 strip text lines, top to bottom (one physical line each, mid-line windows):
  1 ]n amabilis[
  2 ]um nunc[
  3 ]ua pre[
  4 (no visible text)
  5 ]sus iohann[
  6 ]t alleluia [?
  7 P ater [        (large red P)
  8 ]bi nunc [
  9 ]uia Euoua[e
 10 ]alleluia [red rubric letter]
 11 ]altum all[
 12 Euouae S[       (red S)
 13 ]e. adorem[
 14 ]tua sup[

=====================================================================
FACE 4, STRIP (A, reverse side)  -- crops of native tiles, x 60-600
=====================================================================
Much more abraded than face 3 (the side that was pasted down / exposed). Same ruling: red line
per neume row, faint yellow line, text below.

f4strip-033.jpg (from tile image-033.jpg; top of strip, hole at top as on face 3).
 Top ~450 px: blank/abraded, one faint red line segment at l.~400 (left).
 f4strip-033 l.580  : ]n   [illegible]   ſ/f [illegible]  (isolated letters; most of line abraded)
 f4strip-033 l.850  : ]c[?] a (red) [illegible]  (black c with a stroke above, overwritten/adjacent
                       red a with an abbreviation stroke; rest abraded)
 f4strip-033 l.1120 : Ps (red) [illegible]  (red "P" with a small red letter above/after it, read
                       "Ps"? or "PS"; then faint brown traces)
 f4strip-033 l.1420 : ]noui[?] [illegible]  (letters "nou" + minim(s), could be "nom"/"noui";
                       then faint traces)
